title: Nintendo Switch Sports Resort review
text: One of my very favourite things to do in Switch Sports Resort isn't, technically, a sport at all. I can't get enough of Prop Plane's free-play mode, taking to the skies, and watching Wuhu Island do its thing below. Swing past the art museum or the shopping precinct and you'll see all sorts of little people milling around; take a wrong-way dive into a tunnel and here come the cars whizzing on by. Out on the water, racers whip and twirl; on the archipelago's sandiest beaches, holidayers recline in the tropical sun. Fly over the stadiums and sports arenas and you'll see matches in progress - furious bouts of tennis, concentrated swings on golfing greens, or the pin-toppling bustle of bowling - crowds going wild in tandem. And if it's quieter contemplation I want, I can explore the subterranean depths of a volcano, or chart a gently winding path along the river banks, or admire the lighthouse perched on the hill. title: Star Wars Zero Company review
text: It took me longer than I'd like to admit to realise something obvious about Star Wars Zero Company. The fate of its eponymous crew - short of cash, betrayed by the shifting sands of circumstance in a tumultuous wider world, scrambling to just about get the job over the line - is really a lot like that of its developers at Bit Reactor. Furloughed for about a month before the game was released, those staff have clearly hustled and scrapped and fought to the last. And so Zero Company the game bears the signs of its development. In places it feels a little patched together, a little under-ready, a game that launched into the world like a roguish pilot might launch a half-repaired starfighter. The windscreen's rattling, warning lights are flashing, one particularly hirsute engineer is deeply unimpressed at the decision to take off, and nobody knows where that ominous groaning noise is coming from. But somehow she's up. And in the end that's all that counts. Read more

text: I'd nearly forgotten Over the Hill's predecessor, Art of Rally , was a racing game. But that's not meant as a slight. It's just that, for all the happy hours I poured into it, I don't recall doing a single race. Instead, it was the aimless meandering, the soothing rhythms of exploration and absent-minded collectible hunting in its free-roam mode that held me transfixed. So the fact Over the Hill completely jettisons the racing stuff and leans entirely into the meditative bit - it even starts with a golden Buddha statue running you through the basics, which probably tells you everything you need to know - is exactly my kind of thing. title: Next-Gen Xbox Could Be $1,800 And Launch In 2028 – Report
text: A new report sheds more details on Microsoft's plans for new Xbox hardware, including a new handheld device and console, and one of the biggest takeaways is the alleged price. According to Fortune , the Project Helix console could cost between $1,200 and $1,800, unless Microsoft opts to subsidize the cost. The system could launch in 2028, the report said. It's not uncommon for platform-holders to eat some of the cost of a new console and make up the difference with software and services. When the Xbox Series X and S platforms launched in 2020, then-Xbox CEO Phil Spencer said Microsoft was losing as much as $200 on every console it sold. Project Helix might be very expensive. Part of what might be driving up the price for new consoles is the ongoing AI-fueled memory and component shortages. Microsoft itself is one of the biggest proponents of the build-out of all things AI, so its own efforts are contributing to an environment where the next Xbox could be incredibly expensive. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma reacted to this irony, saying it's "wonderful" that GPUs have use beyong gaming. Richer households already made up the majority of console-buyers today , and that trend is expected to continue Additionally, the report said Microsoft might release a "next-generation handheld device" for Xbox by the end of 2027, though there were no details on pricing or anything else. Project Helix is the name for Microsoft's efforts for a "family of devices," so that would seemingly span both console and handheld. The report added that Microsoft's Xbox and Windows teams reportedly battled over what software should run Project Helix, with the Windows team wanting the handheld to use a "trimmed-down" version of Windows Home. The Xbox team, meanwhile, reportedly pushed to build its own dedicated software. An unnamed "senior Xbox executive" was said to have threatened to pull the plug on the entire handheld device rather than use Windows. Going forward, Xbox is "largely controlling the direction" of the handheld's OS, but Sharma told the site that the two teams work together. "We can't build Helix on our own," she said. Sharma took over as Xbox CEO in February this year, immediately declaring that Xbox was in an unhealthy place and taking drastic measures that she believes may right the ship, including laying off staff, closing studios, and cancelling games. The layoffs, which have included about 2,000 people so far , are not done yet, as the Fortune story says more Xbox layoffs are coming this month, in November, and then again in January 2027. Sharma also made major organizational changes, including handing Halo over to Activision for the future .

title: Here Are The Mechanics and Dozens Of New Cards From Magic: The Gathering’s Star Trek Set
text: After a year that featured alternate realities, ninja turtles, superheroes, and hobbits, the final Magic: The Gathering expansion of 2026 is going where no Universes Beyond set has gone before, as Star Trek is scheduled to launch in November. Today, Wizards of the Coast revealed the mechanics players can expect in the set, along with dozens of new cards from both the main set and the preconstructed Commander decks. We also got a glimpse at some of the set's special treatments, including the seven cards that will come signed by the people depicted on the artwork. Here's everything revealed during today's Magic: The Gathering Star Trek debut. The mechanics of MTG Star Trek Seven new mechanics--two of them found only in the Commander cards--highlight the set, along with a eighth mechanic returning from 2024's Edge of Eternities. OPen Communications First is Beam Me Up , which allows you to cast certain spells from your graveyard by returning a creature you control to its owner's hand and paying a separate cost. The example card provided is Open Communications , which normally costs a single blue mana, but you can cast it again from your graveyard by returning a creature to its owner's hand and paying two generic and one blue mana. Next is Face A Dilemma , which adds an additional wrinkle to a mechanic Magic fans are very familiar with. Basically, any time you have to choose a mode in a spell, you are "facing a dilemma," and there are cards in Star Trek that will give extra benefits simply because you made a choice. Seven of Nine , for example, lets you draw a card any time you have to make a choice on a modal spell. Star Trek also introduces new modal spells, like the enchantment Kobayashi Maru Scenario . Every turn after casting this card, you must choose one of the four effects listed on the card, and you can't choose the same one twice--which means if you can't remove the enchantment after four turns, it's game over. The next mechanic is Federation , which cares about the number of creature types among creatures you control that aren't the Borg (which makes sense, because the Federation and the Borg are like oil and water). With Captain Jonathan Archer , by paying one green mana and tapping Archer, you can give another creature +X/+X until end of turn. As Archer is a Human Officer, and he creates a Dog token, that's at minimum +3/+3 on the first activation. Starfleet Academy , meanwhile, allows you to pay five generic mana, tap it, and choose a color to add one mana of that color for every creature type among creatures you control. If you have a wide board of varied tokens, that could be a massive mana source. Strange New Worlds is the next new mechanic, which cares about the lands you control. The more lands with different names you have on the board, the more effective these cards will be. Deep Space Scan , for example, will let you draw a card for each differently named land on your side of the table. If you're playing a three-color deck, and you have an Island, a Mountain, and a Forest on the board, that's three cards coming to your hand. Captain Pike, Fullness of Time , meanwhile, has his power and toughness determined by the number of differently named lands you control. If you're the type of person who likes to play different non-basic lands in your Commander deck, casting Captain Pike late in the game could result in a massive creature on the spot. So far, we've focused on the good guy mechanics, now here's one for the baddies. Assimilate allows you to take any creature from a certain zone and add it to your battlefield, though it will become a Borg artifact creature instead of its other types. Borg Cube lets you exile any creature on the board when it enters, and then when it attacks for the first time, you can add that exiled creature to your board as a Borg. Then, for every subsequent attack, you can repeat the process. Borg Cube also shows off the major returning mechanic, Edge of Eternities' Spacecraft and Station mechanic. Multiple iconic spaceships from Star Trek's history appear on cards in the set, and they all have the Station mechanic, which allows a player to tap a creature in order to add charge counters to the Spacecraft equal to that creature's power. Once enough charge counters are added, the Spacecraft becomes an artifact creature and gains extra abilities. For example, when three charge counters are added to D-7 Battle Cruiser , it will create a 2/1 Klingon Warrior creature token at the beginning of combat on your turn. When eight or more counters are added to it, it becomes a 3/3 flying creature. Worf, Defiant Commander The final two mechanics are exclusive to the Commander format, and only found on cards in the preconstructed commander decks. The first is Battlefront , which grants additional perks based on how many opponents you attack during a combat phase. Worf, Defiant Commander is the face card of the Klingon Fury precon deck, and his Battlefront ability lets you exile a number of cards from the top of your library equal to the number of opponents you attacked. Until your next turn, you can play those cards as if they were in your hand. Now, this ability only cares about players you actively attack. Abilities like myriad, which add tokens to the board already attacking, will not count toward a Battlefront ability, so choose wisely. Jean-Luc Picard, Luminary Seek Out is the other Commander-only mechanic, and it gives an added perk whenever you draw your second card in a turn, even if the permanent with the ability wasn't on the field when you drew your first card. Jean-Luc Picard, Luminary is the example card, as he gives a +1/+1 counter to a creature and two charge counters to a Spacecraft every time you draw your second card in a turn. Booster Fun treatments The Star Trek set will feature many themed treatments across its suite of products, and all of those were shown off during the stream as well. First up are the seven Headliner Signature cards, which feature seven prominent faces from across Star Trek's history. Each of these cards will come with the authentic signature of the actor who portrayed the character; which means you could pull a Levar Burton, Patrick Stewart, Kate Mulgrew, or William Shatner autograph out of a Collector Booster pack, among others. title: Xbox Series X|S Is Getting A Surprise Graphics Boost From AMD
text: Sony isn't the only company introducing new upscaling technology to its flagship PlayStation 5, as Microsoft and AMD have announced that FSR 4.1 is coming to more devices--including Xbox Series X|S consoles--in the future. Similar to Sony's hardware-accelerated upscaling solutions for PS5 and PS5 Pro, AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR) 4.1 is an advanced, machine-learning-based temporal image upscaling and reconstruction technology that can render a game at a lower resolution and then upscale it to a higher resolution. While it's highly doubtful that Xbox Series X|S consoles will start offering PS5 Pro-like graphics (both consoles lack dedicated hardware for machine-learning algorithms), this should still give owners a noticeable bump in graphical quality and performance if implemented properly. "At Xbox, we're building a gaming platform designed to meet players where they are and make it easier for creators to reach them," Xbox chief technology officer Scott Van Vliet said in the announcement video. "AMD has been an important partner in that journey for more than two decades. Together, our teams have been pushing gaming forward, across Xbox and Windows, from the silicon at the heart of our consoles and handhelds to technologies like DirectX, Advanced Shader Delivery, and Auto SR that help developers get more from the hardware and deliver better experiences for our players. Today, we're excited to take another step forward together, with FSR 4.1 coming to Xbox." Van Vliet added that FSR 4.1 will come to Xbox Series X|S "soon," and that Microsoft and AMD are working to bring the tech to the next-gen Xbox console, Project Helix . https://youtu.be/fT6TIXnmv-s Beyond that, AMD didn't share any more details on FSR 4.1 for Xbox Series X|S. FSR 1 and FSR 2 relied primarily on spatial algorithms or basic temporal accumulation to upscale games, and questions remain about who will adopt the technology and add support. Just because the latest version of FSR is out doesn't mean a game will automatically use it. For example, Capcom built the console versions of Pragmata around FSR 1, scaling up from 720p on Xbox Series S and 1080p on Xbox Series X. FSR integration requires manual developer work and testing, so results may vary. We're already seeing signs of this on PS5 with Quick Spectral Super Resolution ; for now, only Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei will support the new AI upscaling upgrade on base PS5 consoles. Essentially, developers will have to actually patch their games to use it; AMD FSR 4.1 will not automatically upgrade every older game overnight. The announcement comes just weeks before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 , and while Rockstar hasn't confirmed if its open-world game will utilize any upscaling technology like PSSR, QSSR, FSR 4.1, we could be looking at a current-gen arms race to find the best console to play the biggest game of the year on. Beyond Xbox hardware, AMD FSR 4.1 will also be supported in Radeon RX 6000-series graphics cards, Gorgon Halo and Strix Halo Ryzen 9 laptops, and mobile gaming PC handhelds like the Asus ROG Xbox Ally devices that use Z2 Extreme and Z2A chipsets.

title: Sony Boss: “Creativity Is For Humans, Not AI”
text: Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick and Sony Group President and CEO, Hiroki Totoki, commented on the future of gaming today at the Paley International Summit. Naturally, the topic of AI came up, and Totoki believes AI technologies will not replace humans in game development, in part because of the creativity required. "Creativity is for humans, not AI,” Totoki said, as reported by IGN . “How to use the technology profile is important. Of course, I encourage my people to use AI in a certain manner, but at [the] same time we try to keep the rights and rights holders and creators and artists.” For his part, Zelnick said it's his belief that AI itself will not replace a developer, but instead, people who don't embrace AI might be replaced by people who do. "I’m fond of saying AI is a collection of datasets, compute, and large language models. That’s what it is. And datasets, by definition, are backward-looking. That’s all they are. And creativity, at its best, is forward-looking," he said. Zelnick said ideas that are "completely unexpected" don't come from algorithms--they come from creative people making surprising, original choices. To make his point, Zelnick said when he was an executive at Fox, he oversaw the release of Home Alone, a movie that no one expected to be a success. "It turned out to be the highest-grossing comedy of all time. So if hits are unexpected, data sets aren’t gonna get you there, no matter how fluent they are," he said. Both PlayStation and Take-Two have embraced AI, with PlayStation heavily leveraging the technology in its game-development processes . As for Take-Two, the publisher is utilizing the technology for its workflows , but there is no AI in GTA 6 . There has been significant pushback for AI in game development from developers and players alike, with many expressing concerns about job security, legal issues, and simply the further "enshi**ification" of everything they love.

title: 10 Years After The Switch 1 Reveal, I Still Haven’t Played A Game At A Rooftop Party
text: It's now been a full decade since Nintendo announced the first Switch, which is almost hard to believe, given how fresh that reveal trailer still feels in our heads. Heaps of hype and a lack of information from Nintendo about its Wii U successor, codenamed "NX," led to the company's fanbase becoming increasingly restless. Reports and rumors pointed to the NX as a console-handheld hybrid , but Nintendo didn't fully unveil the Switch until October 20, 2016 (an announcement preluded by a photo of Mario being a creep ). The three-and-a-half-minute video made it clear how Nintendo wanted players to interact with the Switch, showing several scenarios where people take their games on the go. Rewatching that trailer today, it's amusing to look back at how Nintendo foresaw the social impact of the Switch. Some moments from the trailer manifested in reality, while others were hilariously exaggerated. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iS-1tDfLxRQ You have a guy taking his dog (and his copy of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild) out on a walk, a traveler playing Skyrim on a plane and putting the game on his television upon his arrival home, and professional Splatoon players practicing before their big moment on stage. And then, there's "Nintendo Karen." The most-talked-about moment in the trailer centered on a woman playing Super Mario Odyssey before being prompted to join friends for a rooftop party (a typical gathering of millennials, as people would joke back then), during which she breaks out the Switch, pulls out that dinky little kickstand, and plays a game with a friend as onlookers holding red Solo cups watch with indifference. Fans branded this commercial character as "Karen" and debated the social implications of bringing a Switch to such a function. The Nintendo Switch reveal trailer remains a striking piece of marketing, with its upbeat vibe and extra emphasis on the Switch's branding (much needed, after the Wii U's marketing failures). In the years since the Switch's release, I’ve seen Switches out in the wild, just as Nintendo imagined, though I've yet to go to a rooftop party like the one Karen attended. While the Switch 2 continues to sell well, there's a notion that its reveal was a bit cold and lacking in fanfare compared to the original Switch. Even so, Nintendo still hasn't lost its charm and quirk, even though the company will probably never use that hilarious picture of Mario behind the curtain ever again.

title: Netflix’s Push Into Gaming Continues To Fall Short
text: Netflix has undertaken efforts over the years to increase its footprint in the world of video games, but it's been a bumpy road, and new data suggests that the company is falling short of its targets. According to a Netflix memo seen by The Wall Street Journal , only 3.5% of Netflix's subscribers play games monthly. That's 10% behind Netflix's 2026 target for "reach and engagement" for games, the memo said. In 2022, it was reported that fewer than 1% of Netflix subscribers played games on Netflix . https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uSN_LlaJAXU Getting deeper into games is part of Netflix's effort to increase engagement, and it's not the only measure that Netflix has undertaken. The company has also expanded to live sports and podcasts. Netflix's priorities for gaming have bounced around over the years. At one point in time, Netflix was planning to create AAA games and hired big-name talent. However, Netflix later backtracked , and today the company focuses more on mobile and social games. Recently, co-CEO Ted Sarandos was asked if Netflix will abandon gaming entirely in the future, and he doesn't think the company will , at least not soon. Sarandos said gaming is appealing to Netflix because, for example, someone who just finished a Netflix show can stay engaged with the brand through Netflix's tie-in games connected to those franchises. Beyond tie-in games for Netflix properties like Stranger Things and Love is Blind, Netflix commissions new games like Unhinged and The Conjuring: Unspoken . The streaming giant also made a big play in gaming this year by hosting the GTA 6 Extended Look trailer, and it worked to get people to sign up for Netflix and watch on the platform . Netflix previously worked with Take-Two to bring GTA games to the platform. Red Dead Redemption from Take-Two's Rockstar division remains available to play on Netflix. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1lsV9I2NDO8 These new details about Netflix's efforts in gaming come amidst a big shakeup at the company--a number of top executives were let go, or left, earlier this week ahead of Netflix's latest earnings report today, October 20. Netflix's stock price is down 23% this year and 43% over the past 12 months, and investors called on management to make changes to help the stock go back up. Beyond the executive departures, Netflix laid off 1,000+ people recently, which worked out to about 6% of the company's total workforce; this was the largest round of layoffs in Netflix's history.

title: Justice Is Keeping The GTA 6 Hype At Arm’s Length While Making Its Soundtrack
text: Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just look visually impressive; it also has a killer sound thanks to French electronic music duo Justice. Composing the soundtrack for any game is no easy feat, but with GTA 6 generating an unprecedented amount of hype, the team of Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay are well aware of the expectations that have been placed on them. "Yeah, we are aware of the hype of the game, of course, and the fact that people have been waiting for such a long time," Augé said in an interview with the BBC 1 radio show (via NINE1NINE ). "On the other hand, we are aware, and we see this colossus approaching, and at the same time we see it a bit from the outside. So it was a good way for us also not to let these thoughts come into our minds and not intrude on our minds." As for the overall sound of GTA 6'S soundtrack, Justice says that it pulled from various sources to create a unique "flavor" built around several instruments. While there's a subtle '80s influence in what has been heard so far, Justice says that there's far more to the score than just retro vibes. https://youtu.be/QHbDjL_euB0 "We never really put words on it. 'Oh, we need to make an '80s track,' Augé said. "We knew what we needed to do, and it happened to have this kind of flavor. But at the same time, the sounds are futuristic. Like the guitar, it's not even a guitar; it's a synth, because no guitar could have this type of sound that is very phasey and a bit futuristic." To get an idea of what GTA 6's score will sound like, listen to the game's first single, Flower in a Hurricane. Featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard, the track has already earned 2.8 million plays on YouTube in less than a week, and Justice said they got to work with a dream team of performers to make it a reality. "These are people we've always wanted to work with," de Rosnay said. "We didn't think from the beginning that they would necessarily match together, but it came very naturally, and things happened gradually, and all of a sudden we had made a record with all of them." https://youtu.be/JWxoRY7AFSw Beyond the original soundtrack by Justice, GTA 6 will also offer the "next evolution of in-game radio, and more" through several radio stations and podcasts . The official GTA 6 album will have 34 songs written specifically for the game, including new music from Keith Richards and Travis Scott . title: “The Suits” Made All The Money From Call Of Duty: Black Ops 1 And 2 Ports, OG Dev Says
text: Activision recently released ports of 2010's Call of Duty: Black Ops and 2012's Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 on PlayStation, and they were massive hits. According to a report, the games combined to sell more than 11 million copies on PS4 and PS5. Developer Gavin Goslin, who worked on these games at Treyarch, has reflected on the massive success of these ports and why it feels "bittersweet." Posting on LinkedIn , Goslin said it's amazing to see these games continue to perform well in 2026. It's also a bit sad because the "suits" at Activision are raking in all the money, not the original developers, he said. "I poured my life into those games, spending countless, brutal hours in crunch alongside an incredibly talented team to make sure they were perfect. Seeing our blood, sweat, and tears still dominating the charts in 2026 is amazing, but it's hard to watch the suits rake in giant financial windfalls from our old code while the actual creators don't see a dime of it," he said ( via VGC ). "If executives are getting massive bonuses off the longevity of these classics, that wealth needs to be shared retroactively. Legacy revenue should mean legacy rewards for the devs who survived the crunch to build them." As Goslin mentioned here, the re-releases are not remakes or remasters--instead, they are ports with no new features or significant updates , and that's exactly what fans had been clamoring for. People wanted the games in their original state, and that's what they got. There was significant pent-up demand, too. Before the ports, the only way to play them on PlayStation was to find an old PS3 and go from there, since they were never made available via backwards compatibility on PS4 or PS5. Activision marketing boss Tyler Bahl told The Game Business that, "The Black Ops ports were huge successes. We thought they would do well, we didn’t think they would do that well." Bahl went on to say pent-up demand helped make those ports so successful, and Activision is trying to take learnings from that and apply those lessons to MW4 and future Call of Duty games. The next Call of Duty release is Modern Warfare 4 , which arrives on October 23. After that, Activision has teased that a new sub-franchise is coming .

title: GTA 6 Is 148% Ahead Of This Other Popular AAA Game So Far
text: GTA 6 launches in November, and everyone expects it to be a giant, record-breaking release . But just how big will the release be? Early signs are pointing to an enormous, unprecedented launch, and new data backs that up. Sensor Tower compiled preorder data for some of the biggest games released over the past six years, including Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2022), Diablo 4 (2023), Hogwarts Legacy (2023), and Marvel's Spider-Man (2023). The analysis firm found, as reported by GI.biz , that GTA 6 is beating all of them, and by a very healthy margin. MW2 was the biggest of the bunch in terms of digital preorders, and Sensor Tower said GTA 6 preorders are pacing 148% ahead of MW2's over a comparable period of time before release. This is for digital games only in the US, so it's not a complete picture. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=klc0fQmAL6k Sensor Tower's GTA 6 sales tracker says the game has sold more than 6.45 million copies thus far, generating more than $630 million so far. The company previously said it expects the bulk of preorders to come in the final week before launch, and that total prepurchases could reach 25 million . That would work out to more than $2 billion in revenue, before the game even releases. According to Sensor Tower's data, the majority of preorders for GTA 6 so far are on PS5 (74%), compared to 26% on Xbox Series X|S. This split is no surprise, given that the PS5 has sold much better than the Xbox Series X|S. For its part, Xbox says it is very happy with GTA 6 preorder numbers . GTA 6 is a single-player game, but Rockstar is expected to eventually release the next iteration of GTA Online , and it's expected to be a huge moneymaker. GTA 6 launches on November 19, 2026 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with a PC version potentially following in early 2027 .

title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 Is More Punk Rock Than Blockbuster
text: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season Two once again sees Studio Trigger handle animation duties, and this time, the anime powerhouse has gotten even wilder with its depiction of Night City and its residents. While the first season was bold in its visual direction, director Kai Ikarashi has pushed it even further, using more abstract shapes and experimental animation techniques to capture the look and feel of a cutting-edge dystopia. What does that lead to? A new season that showrunner Bartosz Sztybor calls a shift from Michael Bay-directed movies to Martin Scorsese-inspired (absolute) cinema. "I think the difference for me is—and I think I once made this reference—visually, the first season was very Michael Bay, while this second season is more like Martin Scorsese," Sztybor said to GameSpot. "He uses shapes and light differently. Even if the backgrounds are the same real places from the game, and Studio Trigger was sometimes using the same assets, the way he recreates them is different. It fits the vibe of the story, which is also very different. It's not this huge emotional thing, but rather something indie, more punkish, and more realistic. For example, the violence in season two feels more striking and real to me personally—more shocking, even if it's not as over-the-top as in season one." Ikarashi and Studio Trigger's visual direction for this new season allows for a range of Cyberpunk topics. From cyber-psychosis (where heavily augmented people violently lose their grip on reality) to an all-powerful AI program sharing space with your mind, the result is a series that doesn't look like a stereotypical anime series. Ikarashi has made a name for himself as a key animator on several anime series that have reflected his abstract tastes, like the critically acclaimed Bocchi the Rock, Mob Psycho 100, and Evangelion: 3.0+1.0 Thrice Upon a Time, so if you're familiar with his work, you'll have an idea of what to expect in the new Edgerunners series. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hOwI_kMZ_2o This theme of experimentation also extends to the character Roman, a young cinephile who serves as the point-of-view character in Edgerunners. Always armed with an analogue camera, a large chunk of the show is seen through the low-resolution 4:3 lens of his device. Sztybor added that Roman became a pivotal part of the story after he discovered that both he and Ikarashi were cinephiles. "It was super funny because when I was pitching the story to Studio Trigger, Roman wasn't in the story," Sztybor explained. "While working on the storyline and getting to know Kai Ikarashi better, we discovered that we are both cinephiles and love cinema. We had so many characters and realized we needed a POV character through whom we could see all the others—a connection between them. We thought, 'Okay, we love cinema; let me create a cinephile this season.' Going back to that constant dialogue between two seasons as a mirror: one of the themes of season one was losing innocence. We thought Roman could reference this theme by being a glimpse of innocence in a terrible city. That's why he loves retro things and is against braindances—he wants to maintain that innocence as long as he can." Roman isn't the only cinephile in Night City, as eagle-eyed fans can also spot Hideo Kojima making a cameo in the series. Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 consists of 10 episodes, and it'll be available starting October 20.

title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 Mirrors The First Season, But With One Major Difference
text: Amid all the violence and cool cyborg technology, the first season of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners is a tragic love story at its core. But in the second season? It might be more punk-rock , following a new cast of characters around Night City, but according to showrunner Bartosz Sztybor, emotional themes of love and parenthood are the connective tissue between seasons. "Honestly, from my perspective, all the themes, emotions, and questions are almost the same as with season one," Sztybor said to GameSpot. "I really like to treat both seasons as connected, as mirrors of each other—two pieces of something bigger that have a constant dialogue with each other. It's still a tale about sacrifices and what you will do for love. In season one, we saw the relationship between David and his mother in the first episode, and how the things she told him shaped him. Even in the last episode, he mentions his mom. Season one had this parent-child relationship from the kid's point of view. In the second season, we also have a parent-child relationship, but from the parent's perspective. A lot of those things are connected, but the cast and the choices are different, so the outcomes may also be different. It's like walking into the same river, but choosing a different path." The new season features an overarching storyline split among four characters, each bringing a unique viewpoint to everything happening around them. King is a former Night City legend who has had to downgrade his tech to avoid falling victim to cyber-psychosis; D is a Nomad netrunner out for revenge; and Roman is a young cinephile with barely any cybernetic enhancements. The young Talia, a Maelstrom gang member who has heavily modified her body, becomes the group's focal point as they find themselves drawn into a web of intrigue revolving around illegal technology, warring corporations, and even a lingering plot thread from the first season of Edgerunners. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hOwI_kMZ_2o "It was in the first pitch that Talia was the main point of conflict for everyone, and we slowly built things around her," Sztybor added. I knew King would be her father and an old Edgerunner wanting to rebuild that relationship. Then we thought she needed to be connected to Maelstrom, super-chromed, and special in a way that connects her to [the AI superweapon] Capri and then to D. It was a puzzle from the start. I knew from the moment I thought about Edgerunners 2 that I wanted it to be like Tarantino's Pulp Fiction—a few characters who eventually connect. What they share is that they don't fit the system and are unhappy with who they are, except Roman, who has that glimpse of hope." Could there be a third season of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners? Sztybor is taking things one day at a time, but one thing is for sure: if it enters production, you can expect more threads from the wider Cyberpunk 2077 universe to be woven into it. "I don't know if there will be a perfect story," Sztybor said about a potential third season." Of course, there are a lot of stories to tell. I love worldbuilding and connecting characters, places, or elements from comic books and the game." "In Edgerunners 2, there's Sal Bigelow, a character who was shown earlier in the Cyberpunk: Big City Dreams comic book. The main goal is to show that this world is alive, and all these characters have their stories, agendas, and very often sad endings. To answer your question about season three: let's see, but there are definitely more stories to tell in this world." Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 is now out on Netflix with 10 new episodes. For more on the show, check out how its anime talent radically changed Edgerunners' style , and yes, there is a quick Hideo Kojima cameo hiding in the middle of the season.

title: WoW: Forever Is Soaring, But Midnight Is Struggling
text: World of Warcraft : Forever is riding high thanks to its popular beta and upcoming launch, but retail WoW's Midnight expansion feels like it's in a state of crisis by comparison. The two different versions of WoW couldn't be in more different places. Forever seems to be extremely popular, with Blizzard developers commenting how its beta is breaking records . Blizzard itself has also been more communicative regarding Forever than ever before, with weekly podcasts diving into community topics, forum posts addressing various issues, and frequent updates addressing balance problems and bugs. Midnight seems to be in the opposite corner. Its latest content update, patch 12.1.5, went live October 13. In addition to new story quests that continue the expansion's main narrative, it added a new single-boss raid and a long-teased mega delve (officially called a labyrinth) that gives solo-focused players an almost raid-like experience. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=phxy5Gat_Gs Unfortunately, the patch was released in a bug-riddled state. The Kindo'jan labyrinth, arguably the patch's biggest feature, saw players running into issue after issue. Some players complained about not earning credit for boss kills and being unable to collect rewards. One particularly nasty bug had players falling through the floor of the labyrinth's final boss arena, making it so the labyrinth couldn't be completed. Other players cited issues with delve companion Valeera dying too quickly or failing to do proper boss mechanics. Many of the most glaring bugs (like falling through the floor) were fixed in a hotfix deployed on October 16, but labyrinths still have a major issue: no save points . When Blizzard first detailed labyrinths, it implied players would be able to start one, make some progress, and come back to finish it at a later time. Blizzard's exact wording was that players would be able to "venture through them in a single epic session or tackle them piece by piece over time, progressing at your own pace." That currently isn't true, as the labyrinth has no checkpoints and must be completed in a single session. Labyrinths taking at least an hour or so to complete, combined with various bugs preventing progress and no way to save and come back to them later, is making for an incredibly frustrating experience. It's unclear if the lack of checkpoints is a bug, an unannounced change on Blizzard's part, or just some kind of oversight, but it's not a great debut for Midnight's newest feature. Story spoilers for WoW: Midnight patch 12.1.5 below. Bugs and issues surrounding labyrinths are just one part of why patch 12.1.5 has proven unpopular. The patch is also catching flak for its story, specifically how it killed off a major character unceremoniously. Liadrin, a blood elf paladin and one of the main characters players have interacted with over the course of Midnight, dies facing off against Kithix, the resurrected Old God general that serves at the patch's new raid encounter. However, she doesn't die in any kind of epic or heroic way. Instead, judging from the post-raid cinematic, she dies from what seems to be exhaustion, having wielded the power of the light too strongly in the battle against Kithix. After Kithix's defeat, Liadrin utters "Darkness will never prevail" before crumpling to the ground and dying. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u9SH-vKAy1Y WoW is not a stranger to having major characters die. It famously happened with Varyian Wrynn, the leader of the Alliance, during the start of the game's Legion expansion. But unlike Varyian's epic death, Liadrin's feels anticlimactic. The fact that it occurs during a .5 patch that feels disconnected to the game's larger narrative makes the story beat feel unnecessary. Adding salt to the wound is that her death looks to be in service of a recurring and unpopular trend in recent WoW storylines where old rivalries and feuds between factions are easily reconciled. In Liadrin's case, her death brings together the blood elves and the Amani trolls, though Blizzard does make a point in a post-raid quest to emphasise the two groups are not allies despite now being at peace. Blizzard may have said its putting the "war" back in Warcraft during BlizzCon 2026, but all of its recent story beats have seen ancient enemies coming together and cooperating, and Liadrin's death only serves to reinforce that. This isn't the first time a .5 patch has been met with negative reception from WoW's players. It was only back in April that Blizzard released patch 12.0.5 in an extremely buggy state . Player outcry saw Blizzard go as far to issue a public apology , stating it was "taking lessons learned from this launch to help ensure this doesn't happen again," and that "we will do better." Flash forward six months later, and it doesn't seem like much has changed. That puts Midnight in a weird place overall. Blizzard barely talked about modern WoW at this year's BlizzCon. It teased Midnight's final content patch that will see players finally confront Xal'atath once and for all, but didn't share more details about what to expect from the game's next expansion, The Last Titan, despite it being slated to release next year. Instead, Blizzard put almost all its emphasis on WoW: Forever, a new, WoW Classic-inspired version of Blizzard's MMORPG that adds new content and visual upgrades to the old-school version of Azeroth. In an interview with GameSpot, Blizzard shared more details on what to expect from WoW: Forever's future and its endgame. WoW: Forever launches November 4.

title: You Don’t Need An Expensive Console Or High-End PC To Play Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
text: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 releases this week, and with gaming consoles and capable PC rigs now more expensive than ever, you might be wondering if there is another way to play. Thankfully, there is, but there are a few things you need to know before jumping in. How to play MW4 without a console or PC With Game Pass: Modern Warfare 4 is not included with Xbox Game Pass this year, but if you're a subscriber you can leverage the "stream your own game" program to play it that way, after purchasing it outright. This isn't locked away to any specific tier of Game Pass, either. You can subscribe to Game Pass Essential, Premium, or Ultimate to stream MW4. MW4 launches on October 23. With GeForce Now: Nvidia's streaming service, GeForce Now, will be another way to play Modern Warfare 4 without any expensive hardware like a new console or high-end PC. Or at least we think so. Nvidia hasn't outright confirmed this, but people are playing the campaign early access via GeForce Now , so it stands to reason that it will be officially supported at launch for everyone. After buying the game outright, you'll be able to stream MW4 on GeForce Now by subscribing to one of the platform's membership tiers. GeForce Now has multiple tiers, including a free ad-supported membership. There are also $10/month and $20/month tiers with no ads and higher-fidelity experiences. There are also day passes available. For more, check out the GeForce Now website . Pros and cons of streaming Before subscribing to Game Pass or GeForce Now, people should know that playing a twitch shooter like Modern Warfare 4 over the internet might not always be the perfect experience. After all, a cloud service works best with a strong and stable connection, and that's not always a guarantee. However, many people report good experiences, and as always, your mileage may vary. Something else to consider is that, starting in November, Microsoft will implement caps on how many hours people can stream via Game Pass before they must pay more to keep playing. The benefits of streaming are pretty obvious: You don't need any expensive hardware. This is because a game is streamed on high-end hardware and beamed to your screen, whatever that may be. You will still need a controller or a keyboard and mouse setup, but you might have those things already, and if you don't, they cost significantly less than a new console or a powerful PC. Why are consoles and PCs so expensive today? The Xbox Series X|S and PS5 consoles were released in 2020, but today, six years later, they are more expensive than ever. Historically, console prices come down instead of going up. So what's driving the price increases? The AI-fueled demand for components and memory is to blame, as is the war in Iran that's driving up oil prices. There are numerous other macroeconomic factors at play, too, including tariffs. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FatSqS3VYY Companies like Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo want to keep making money in this environment. Instead of eating the costs (while they make huge profits and collect tariff refunds), they are charging people more to maintain their margins. The Switch 2 is among the cheapest ways to play MW4 this year, with that console starting at $500 (up from $450 at launch). The PS5 now starts at $600 (up from $400 at launch) and the latest Xbox consoles are more expensive, too. The Series S now goes for $500 (was $300) and Series X for $750 ($500 at launch). In short, you're in for major sticker shock if you're buying a new console. For PC players, it's more expensive than ever to build a capable rig, but your price will vary depending on the setup you want, preconfigured or made yourself. For more, check out GameSpot's Modern Warfare 4 campaign review , and keep checking back for more coverage on DMZ and multiplayer when the game goes live on October 23.

title: This LA Noire Spinoff Idea Sounds Incredible
text: British actor Rahul Kohli (Saros, Midnight Mass) has a pitch for a new L.A. Noire game, and it sounds pretty great. Speaking to BAFTA Games , Kohli said he would like to see the franchise return with a spinoff that takes players through different time periods, as a cop, as they investigate different crimes. One such setting could be Victorian England, with a storyline focused on hunting down Jack the Ripper, Kohli said. Another could take players to the '80s in California as they pursue the Night Stalker, the actor added. "We could jump around and be a cop in different times. I would be down for that," Kohli said. "I loved it. I adored L.A. Noire." Mad Men's Aaron Staton as Cole Phelps in L.A. Noire. In particular, Kohli said he was a big fan of developer Team Bondi's facial-capture system which created lifelike expressions in the game, down to granular details like how a person’s eyebrows might move. In a game where players had to read people's facial expressions, this was a big deal, and one can only imagine how much further the technology could go today. However, Kohli said he wants a new L.A. Noire game with the same tech and the same engine. "I want that. I don't want an improvement to it. That was part of the charm," he said. https://twitter.com/BAFTAGames/status/2112216181440745623 L.A. Noire was released in 2011. It never got a sequel, and its developer, Team Bondi, later disbanded. A virtual reality game, L.A. Noire: The VR Case Files, was released in 2017. Earlier this year, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick said the company was looking at future projects in all of its franchises , and that includes L.A. Noire. Back in 2012, Rockstar said a sequel to L.A. Noire was a “possibility.” At the time, the developer said, “We don’t always rush to make sequels, but that does not mean we won’t get to them eventually. We have so many games we want to make, and the issue is always one of bandwidth and timing.” Recently, a rumor emerged that a new L.A. Noire game is now in the works, and it will have players collecting clues to try to find the Zodiac Killer .

title: Mr. Beast’s Call Of Duty: MW4 DMZ Video Pays $1 Million To The Winner, Watch It Here
text: YouTube star Mr. Beast, who has more than 500 million subscribers on that platform alone, has published a Call of Duty video today, October 19, to mark the release of Modern Warfare 4. title: Saros Gets Boss Rush And Tons Of Difficulty Options With Zenith Update
text: Saros is a phenomenal sci-fi shooter, and it currently stands as my favorite game of 2026. If you've been waiting for the right time to play it--or to play it again--then developer Housemarque has some good news. The new Zenith update is now available for free, adding a boss rush and difficulty options that should appeal to both newcomers and seasoned veterans. First up, the boss rush. Dubbed "Overlord Rush," the mode comes with its own dedicated leaderboards and tasks you with taking out a series of the game's bosses. Rather than starting on the first boss and fighting uninterrupted to the very end, they're divided into separate "sets" that each contain three fights. Overlord Rush is available via the Primary robot in the main hub area. https://youtu.be/X3SsUZ1SFy4 The new settings and difficulty modifiers, meanwhile, allow you to both reduce and increase the game's challenge, customizing it to fit your preferences. The "Slow Game Speed" setting lets you slow down the entire game so you have more time to react to projectiles, and you can tweak exactly how much it slows down and even if you want it to turn on automatically when combat starts. An "Auto-fire" setting also eliminates the need to actually pull the trigger when you aim, which can be handy when you're primarily focused on dodging incoming attacks. You can think of it almost like a Vampire Survivors-style tool. Carcosan Modifiers were already in the game at launch, giving you the choice to make the game easier or harder--or a mix of both in different parts of the game--but a whole bunch more were added with Zenith. New Protection modifiers include a "Corruption Melee Enhancement," as outlined on the PlayStation Blog , which gives your melee attacks more power if you acquire Corruption, which is typically not a good thing to have. Trial Modifiers, meanwhile, make the game more challenging, and when combined with the new ultra-hard endgame Eclipse Layers, you'll be able to put all your skills to the test. Saros is available exclusively on PS5. In our Saros review , Richard Wakeling called it an "incredible game that does more than just refine what worked before."

title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer’s Biddy Blas Is Voiced By A Sinister Circus Ringmaster Pro Wrestler, And This Makes Sense
text: Star Wars has had no shortage of breakout alien stars over the decades--from Chewbacca in the original trilogy to Grogu from The Mandalorian--but in Star Wars: Galactic Racer, that honor belongs to Biddy Blas. Who is Biddy Blas? A hotshot racer in the game, with an ego the size of a Death Star and a voice that sounds like a TIE Fighter fueled by nightmares— that's who Biddy Blas is. And in real life, the man behind the voice is none other than indie UK wrestler and actor Richard Summers-Calvert, who is down to "scrib doon" some autographs from fans. Performing under the name "The Spectacular Tw*t" Charles Crowley, Summers-Calvert has popped up in multiple pro wrestling promotions, including a recent appearance in Ring of Honor. The actor and wrestler says he's been humbled by Biddy Blas's popularity since he was introduced in Star Wars: Galactic Racer. "I could tell Biddy Blas was gonna be popular early on," Summers-Calvert said to Soundsphere . "Then I woke up the next day and he'd blown up a bit, and then the next day it kind of dawned on me that this isn’t normal." https://www.instagram.com/p/DemxqBbp7DO/ Since then, Summers-Calvert says he has received a ton of messages, mentions, and even "Biddy Blas thirst traps" online. For the role, Summers-Calvert recalled that the audition called for a small man who was constantly on the edge and overcompensating, which convinced the pro wrestler to raise his pitch. The game directors liked it, but the role wasn't easy--especially when he had to perform his lines in the Star Wars language of Huttese. "I keep seeing online people talking about like cuteness aggression, and they love him so much they want to throw him at the wall," Summers-Calvert added. The popularity of Biddy Blas has only grown in recent weeks, as the character has been referenced in numerous memes and even by sports teams, like the Pittsburgh Steelers: https://twitter.com/steelers/status/2111957158267138184 For pro wrestling fans, it's another example of how the theatrical side of sports entertainment has naturally connected with video games. Roman Reigns, who plays Akuma in the new Street Fighter movie, recently commented on the power of video games and how performers prefer to spend their downtime between shows with a console. Other wrestlers like Kenny Omega have also incorporated video games into their movesets and personas, referencing their favorite titles as signature attacks in the ring. At this rate, don't be too surprised if a Wrestler starts hitting his opponents with the "Scrib Doon" finisher. If you haven't checked it out yet, Star Wars: Galactic Racer is now available for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S. It's pretty great, blending Burnout- and Wipeout-inspired speed with a well-designed roguelite core that makes every race feel challenging and dangerous.

title: Star Wars Games Could Get More Interesting As Lucasfilm Looks Beyond The Big Studios
text: This year has seen the launch of two Star Wars games, with each one offering a new take on a galaxy far (far!) away. Bit Reactors' Star Wars Zero Company puts its best XCOM foot forward with an aggressive take on turn-based tactics, while Fuse Games' Star Wars Galactic Racer has been hailed for its superb roguelite racing, slick presentation, and the delightful Biddy Blas . Both games have been well received by critics and fans alike, and Lucasfilm Games has been paying attention to the success these independent studios have achieved. "It very much is part of the strategy," Lucasfilm Games VP Douglas Reilly said to The Game Business Show . "Obviously, huge AAA games like Battlefront are always going to be an essential part of the strategy. But one of the great things about Star Wars is it has all kinds of other opportunities to tell stories in different genres. The goal has been to find the best partner to bring that experience to life inside the galaxy far, far away. And it doesn’t have to always be AAA; sometimes it can be AA, and it’s really about the experience that we’re delivering and the fantasy we’re fulfilling." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eA3BrR245mo&pp=0gcJCUMMAYcqIYzv Reilly added that Lucasfilm Games wants to be more flexible in choosing who it partners with to create more Star Wars titles, and some of those studios will "surprise" people when they're eventually revealed. As Reilly put it, Lucasfilm Games isn't looking for a "top five publisher," but rather teams that can meet their expectations for a high-quality title. Even if the developer hasn't established a track record yet, having experienced members on staff can help. Fuse Games is a good example: it was founded by former Criterion Games developers who worked on EA's Burnout and Need for Speed series, as well as the two Star Wars: Battlefront games at the publisher. That's not to say that AAA Star Wars games can't be successful, as the Battlefront series has been hugely popular --controversial lootboxes and all--and as of 2019, they'd sold through 33 million units combined. Konami has also experienced success in recent years by entrusting the Silent Hill franchise to developers outside of its corporate borders. Between Bloober Team, NeoBards Entertainment, and Screen Burn Interactive, Silent Hill has been on a hot streak over the last couple of years. As for future Star Wars games , one of the biggest ones in development is the single-player RPG Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic . Like Zero Company and Galactic Racers, it's being produced by a brand-new developer, Arcanaut Studios, under the direction of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic and Mass Effect veteran Casey Hudson.

title: Open-World Crime Game Samson Did Better On Console But Not Enough To Save Its Developer From Shutting Down
text: Liquid Swords, the Swedish developer behind the crime game Samson , is closing up shop. Founder Christofer Sundberg confirmed this after bankruptcy reports emerged, stating directly, "Liquid Swords is closing." Samson launched on PC in April, but the console edition for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S that released in September "did far better," Sundberg said. However, he admitted that, "It wasn't enough to save the studio." At the same time, Samson might have a future after Liquid Swords closes up shop, the executive said. https://twitter.com/CHSundberg/status/2112186074734752089 "I’m proud of our team and what we built. We’re discussing continued support for Samson. We make mistakes, we learn, we rise, we move on. I never give up. More soon," he wrote. According to a report , all 27 employees at Liquid Swords are being let go as part of the bankruptcy process. Workers reported not getting paid for two months, but those salaries will be covered by local laws in Sweden. Liquid Swords described itself as a "zero-nonsense" game studio. Sundberg said, "Game development has become so full of distractions that affect quality and motivation." He said his ambition was to "change that" with Liquid Swords through eliminating crunch and "useless" meetings, and not taking on an "unnecessary stakeholders." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5B2_jeY0eXQ In the end, this plan did not work out, and Samson will be Liquid Swords' one and only release. Sundberg co-founded Just Cause studio Avalanche and spent more than a decade there before leaving to start Liquid Swords. Sundberg is known for his hot takes on the gaming industry, including a very bleak outlook on the state of gaming today .

title: Battlefield 6 Dev Owns Up To Mistakes With Strange-Looking Cosmetics, But Stays Silent On Possible AI Use
text: Battlefield Studios has released a statement regarding Battlefield 6 after players came together to point out oddities and irregularities with some of the game's newest cosmetics, leading many to openly wonder whether they were the result of generative AI. The developer’s statement admits mistakes with some of the newly released cosmetics, but it did not say whether genAI played a role. Battlefield Studios said it's aware of the "conversation, memes, and candid feedback" about some of Battlefield 6's new skins and cosmetic items. In particular, fans pointed out that a McNeil skin says "SECUTY" on the shoulder instead of "SECURITY." Battlefield Studios is planning to release an update to address this with the Season 5, Phase 2 patch in November. https://twitter.com/BattlefieldInte/status/2110081537882341869 "However, we recognize that letting a known visual error go live without quick acknowledgement creates confusion and erodes trust. We are reviewing how we communicate known visual bugs so you aren’t left wondering whether something was intentional or overlooked," the developer said. Battlefield Studios went on to say it takes pride in "the craft of our world and our gear," and acknowledged that this item missed the mark and does not reflect the developer's own quality standards. "Seeing visual oddities slip through is frustrating for everyone. We are currently examining our internal processes and workflows to pinpoint how these issues occurred and to see how we can tighten our quality control process going forward," the developer said. Battlefield Studios also addressed the Midnight Mirage skin design that gives the character five pistols--you can see this below. The developer said this was an intentional creative choice to reflect the "over-the-top action movie tropes" where soldiers inexplicably always seem to have another weapon strapped to their gear. "That said, we understand how this could look unintentional when released alongside other cosmetic anomalies. As we continue to try out new ideas to see what interests the community, you help us continue to evolve our cosmetics in Battlefield. Thank you for your continued feedback and support," the studio said. https://twitter.com/BattlefieldInte/status/2110053463916683767 When Battlefield 6 launched in 2025, people immediately spotted what they thought were AI-created assets , and Battlefield Studios never denied this. The higher-ups at Battlefield Studios are big believers in AI for game development. While Battlefield Studios may not have acknowledged using AI for in-game assets in Battlefield 6, Activision freely admits to using the technology to create some of its own assets, including with the upcoming Modern Warfare 4. Brandon Stirrup, who works on the business strategy team at Microsoft for Xbox, said recently that companies using AI in 2026 in their workflows is standard practice across numerous industries, including gaming. He said gamers express "negative sentiment" about it, so developers don't always freely admit to using the tech. "Everyone else accepts reality," he said. https://twitter.com/brandonstirrup/status/2111972632115708231 https://twitter.com/brandonstirrup/status/2111991783785644420 In other Battlefield 6 news, the game was recently added to Xbox Game Pass , and it's marked down on all platforms to celebrate the recent Season 5 launch.

title: After 16 Years, Chill Sci-Fi Game Faraway Has A Release Date
text: After more than a decade of development, developer Steph Thirion's chill sci-fi game has a release date of locked in. GameSpot can exclusively reveal that Faraway will launch on November 5 for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Switch consoles. See on Steam Designed to be a tour of the cosmos that you can play with just one button, Faraway was first announced all the way back in 2010, and it follows a shooting star on its journey across the cosmos. Billed as an endless procedurally generated arcade game, the goal is to create constellations on your trek across the stars, using their gravity to slingshot your way to new destinations and keep your cosmic traveler fueled up for the trials that lie ahead of it. Every run starts from zero, while the universe around you is generated in real time based on your overall performance. As you become more skilled, you'll pick up speed, points, and travel to increasingly difficult regions of the universe. The game also includes 16 handcrafted puzzle stages where you'll have to think out of the galactic box, and it's aiming to be a relaxing mix of discovery, replayability, and long-term mastery. Faraway is being published by Annapurna Interactive, a company that has made a name for itself by focusing on games with a strong artistic vision . It also published Forever Ago and last month saw the release of the critically acclaimed Silent Hill: Townfall . Looking ahead, the label will also publish games like the fantasy adventure Demi and the Fractured Dream, the stylish hidden-object game Uncanyon, and the action-RPG We Kill Monsters.

title: Xbox Game Pass Is Losing 8 More Games In October
text: It's that time of month when Xbox updates the Game Pass library, and, as usual, a few more games are leaving the subscription service in a few weeks. On October 31, you can say goodbye to 8 more games, including a few LucasArts classics, a diggy-diggy blast of co-op fun, and one of the biggest Lego Star Wars games of all time. With Double Fine no longer part of the Xbox Game Studios family, it looks like two of the studio's best remasters will be leaving soon. The remastered editions of Full Throttle and Day of the Tentacle are on their way out, so if you haven't checked out these classic '90s point-and-click adventures, now is a great time to do so. Each one features high-resolution artwork and remastered audio. You'll also want to grab the action-packed co-op shooter Deep Rock Galactic , the strategic RPG Wartales , and the PvPvE multiplayer shooter Wildgate , which fuses ship-to-ship combat with fast-paced action. Dead Static Drive is a hidden gem best described as Grand Theft Cthulhu, while Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris is a top-notch co-op game that lets even more players join the intrepid archaeologist on her expeditions. Finally, Lego Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga is a massive game that covers all nine movies in the classic sci-fi series, and like a bucket of Lego, it can keep you entertained for hours. Leaving Xbox Game Pass on October 31 Full Throttle Remastered Dead Static Drive Wildgate Deep Rock Galactic Day of the Tentacle Remastered Wartales Full Throttle Remastered Lego Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris As a reminder, you can save 20% on these games if you decide to buy them before they leave Game Pass. At the start of the month , nine games left Xbox Game Pass, with the critically acclaimed Expedition 33: Clair Obscur as the biggest departure. Other notable exits included The Casting of Frank Stone, A Plague Tale: Requiem, Donut County, and Evil West.

title: Street Fighter Lands A Number One Debut, But Its Box Office Punch Is Weaker Than Expected
text: Street Fighter got off to an okay start on the weekend, punching its way to a $31 million opening at the US box office and a number one debut. That's below the domestic opening weekend of Mortal Kombat 2 earlier this year ($38.5 million), and globally, it made $20.1 million. That brings the worldwide start to $51.1 million so far, well below the original estimate of $70 million for the action movie. During early Thursday results, Street Fighter got off to a $4 million start at the US box office, per Deadline . That's below Mortal Kombat 2's Thursday start ($5.2 million), but for perspective, Sonic the Hedgehog made even less on its first day ($3 million) and still became a hit. Could Street Fighter follow the same trajectory? This first weekend should be a solid indicator if it's a hit or a miss. Street Fighter is the second movie based on a Capcom IP to make its way to the silver screen this year--following Zach Cregger's Resident Evil film in September--but early estimates for the martial arts extravaganza hinted at an uphill battle for it. Typically, movies need to make at least double their production budget back to be considered successful, and with Street Fighter costing $82 million to produce, it doesn't look like it'll recoup its expenses in its first weekend. There's still a chance it could be a small hit if word of mouth drives audiences to theaters, and in terms of competition, Street Fighter has a few weeks to dominate cinemas as it'll be the biggest action film on the block--at least until the November 1 re-release of V for Vendetta, which is celebrating its 20th anniversary. The movie won't open in the potentially lucrative market of China, but internationally, the lion's share of sales is expected to come from Mexico, Brazil, the UK, Australia, and Asian markets. https://youtu.be/U6sbm1OaJb8 How does that opening stack up against other recent video game movie adaptations? Resident Evil got off to a solid start with a $60 million domestic opening last month, and so far, the film has grossed $324 million worldwide, making it a surprise commercial hit and Cregger's biggest film yet . Meanwhile, Mortal Kombat 2 did much worse when it launched in May, making only $38 million on its opening US weekend and finishing with a worldwide box office total of $129.5 million. As for the other Street Fighter movies, they've had mixed results. According to Box Office Mojo , the first Street Fighter movie starring Jean-Claude Van Damme made $99.4 million during its run, which is pretty great for a 1994 flick, but 2009's Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li was a huge flop. It had an opening weekend of $4.7 million in the US, and it made $12.7 million worldwide. "The latest attempt at bringing Capcom's iconic franchise to the big screen has its moments but is mostly messy and largely forgettable," Lisa Wallen wrote in GameSpot's Street Fighter movie review . title: Tenebris Somnia Blends 2D Visuals With Live-Action Horror Scenes, And It’s Already On Sale At Launch
text: Horror games live or die by their scares and tension. If the player isn’t uncomfortable guiding a character through dreadful situations, well, you may as well be playing an action-adventure game (don’t mention the first Uncharted’s final act, please). Tenebris Somnia blends the discomfort of retro horror with live-action sequences that will make your goosebumps bump, and you can get it cheaper than ever right now. As the best horror games continue to push for more realistic visuals and immersive experiences, Tenebris Somnia’s twist on the genre combines old-school cool with movie-like cutscenes. It’s both jarring and original, and that’s exactly what makes for excellent horror. I want to be constantly surprised, and Tenebris Somnia makes its pixelated 2D threats even more menacing when you see live-action versions of the monsters. Inspired by classics that scared us silly, like Resident Evil and Silent Hill, Tenebris Somnia has a deceptively simple premise. You play as Julia, who finds herself in a parallel universe while visiting her ex-boyfriend and is relentlessly hunted by nightmares that, well, aren’t exactly figments of her imagination. (To be honest, visiting an ex sounds like a nightmarish experience on its own. Ba-dum, tsss.) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A_fQ_gNddbo Co-created by Andrés Borghi and Tobías Rusjan with Saibot Studios, and published by New Blood Interactive, the studio behind Ultrakill, Blood West, and Gloomwood, Tenebris Somnia’s style is fittingly inspired by past eras of console gaming.
